bucket_reason: Confidence is still med after corner_rules_2. Every corner event on H* orbits is ruled now and the closure target is met, but the clause for short right ends (block seeds) is wider than what the machine produces, so H*c2 is not yet an inductive invariant.
question: Fund one stage to replace #16's seed clause by closed forms of the short (S) transitions, so that H*c2 becomes inductive, before proof.md?

options.label: One seed-clause stage
options.consequence: About 2 h, 1-2 light processes, no Coq. Derive the S transitions (collapse completion by cascade and edge-mode eats; Absorb starts) in closed form from the macro rules, state the short right ends they produce as linear relations, replace the seed clause of H*c2 with them, and rerun the closure tests including random short seeds drawn from the new clause. Also rule or exclude V1 with d = 1 and Z nonempty. Exits: closed with 0 leaks -> proof.md; a seed family that needs non-linear relations -> park.

options.label: Write proof.md now
options.consequence: Start the hub-to-hub induction on H*c2 with the macro rules as lemmas (Conv/Transfer from TM5's P/P_S/P_S'). The seed clause and the V1 d = 1, Z nonempty case stay as open lemmas.

options.label: Park
options.consequence: Status becomes parked at corner_rules_2. macro_sim3, the CORNER2 rules and the closure tests stay in scripts/ and notes.md.

rationale: Closure target met: 10,000/10,000 orbits at both scales by validated rules; 0 halts.
Left: 29/10^4 random short H* seeds leave; seeds the machine makes stay in.
S transitions are chains of validated rules, so the fix is linear.

evidence.text: CORNER2 rules by exact simulation: 11 families 40/40 each; negative controls 0/110.
No margin, 40 traversals: 10,000/10,000 orbits ruled and in H*c2 at levels <= 5,459 (and <= 1e30); 0 halts.
Random short H* seeds (runs >= 1,000, levels <= 1e30): 9,971/10,000 stay in H*c2; 27 P-mode ends with P even, 2 band k = 2.
End-to-end vs accel_sim through the new rules: 30 orbits, 238 right ends in order, 0 mismatches.
